# `lom405` golden fixture — qiskit-metal tutorial 4.05

The P0-B assembly layer (`quantum_dsl.dsl.assemble`) is validated end-to-end against
qiskit-metal's **New LOM (LOM 2.0)** tutorial *4.05 — New LOM and Two Coupled Transmon
Example*, which is a ready-made golden case: two independently extracted capacitance
matrices, stitched through one shared node name, plus published reference outputs.

## Files

| File | Origin |
|---|---|
| `Q1_TwoTransmon_CapMatrix.txt` | **verbatim copy** of the upstream tutorial input (Ansys Q3D export, transmon "alice") |
| `Q2_TwoTransmon_CapMatrix.txt` | **verbatim copy** of the upstream tutorial input (transmon "bob") |
| `expected.yaml` | generated — parsed inputs + reference outputs, see below |
| `generate_expected.py` | the generator (reference env only; not collected by pytest) |

Upstream path (this machine): `~/metal/qiskit-metal/tutorials/4 Analysis/A. Core - EM
and quantization/`. Notebook: `4.05 New LOM and Two Coupled Transmon Example.ipynb`.

## `expected.yaml`

Generated by re-running the notebook headlessly in conda env `quantum-metal`
(quantum-metal 0.7.6 editable from `~/metal/qiskit-metal`, scqubits 4.3.1):

```
conda run -n quantum-metal python tests/fixtures/lom405/generate_expected.py
```

The generator path + versions are recorded in the file's `provenance` block. It
contains:

* `cells[]` — the **already parsed** Maxwell matrices (post `node_rename`) with their
  terminal name order, plus the verbatim `node_rename` / `ind_dict` / `jj_dict` /
  `cj_dict`. Parsing the Q3D txt is P0-C's job, so `tests/test_assemble.py` reads the
  numbers from here instead of re-implementing a reader.
* `assemble` — the verbatim `grd_node` / `nodes_force_keep`.
* `reference` — `C_n` (accumulated node-basis matrix, ground removed, `cj` folded in),
  `C` (node-junction basis), `C_k` / `C_inv_k` (eq 7b Schur), `L_inv_k`,
  `get_nodes_keep()` / `get_nodes_remove()`, the transmon `EJ`/`EC` (MHz), the
  diagonalized `fQ_in_Ghz` / `chi_in_MHz`, and `compute_gs()`.

⚠ qiskit-metal's constants are CODATA-2014 (`e=1.60217657e-19`, `h=6.62606957e-34`);
`quantum_dsl.dsl.circuit_model` uses exact SI-2019. That is a ~2e-7 relative offset on
`E_C` — four orders of magnitude below the 0.1 % acceptance band, but it is why the
`E_C` comparison is not bit-exact.

## Regenerating

Only needed if the upstream tutorial changes. Re-run the command above;
`expected.yaml` is rewritten in place. The generator needs the **reference** env
`quantum-metal` — never `metal-env` (that one has qiskit-metal 0.5.1, no
`lom_core_analysis`).
